tasks.short: Develop transportation software or computer processes

steps.what: State the computer processes to build
Write tests for those computer processes
Draft software for the named processes

loop.output: a code draft that names only those tests
loop.check: Each drafted function is named by an acceptance test id
loop.stop: One draft, then stop. If a test has no id, return no code
loop.why_not_simpler: Branch logic in the process is free text and a fixed template cannot write it

steps.what: Run tests for the drafted software
Review the software and sign a version
Apply only the signed software version

tasks.design: The traffic analyst states the process, the fields and sample rows on a {WORKFLOW} form. The transportation engineer writes the acceptance tests in {DOCS} first. A bounded draft may propose code, and the engineer reviews the change. Named tests can run on the {DATA_PLATFORM}. A run that finishes is not acceptance. Only the signed version is applied, and only to the internal calculation aid.
tasks.previous_blocker: The process lived in a notebook and the checks lived in the engineer's head, so a draft could not be tied to a named test.
tasks.enabler_now: Input fields, output fields and a sample row can be required before any code is drafted.
tasks.still_hard: Whether the process is the right one, and whether the change is safe to keep, is still a review. A green test is not that review.
tasks.human_edge: The transportation engineer writes the tests, reads the change and signs the version.
tasks.altitude: First drafts take less retyping. The review does not shrink to a test log. The engineer can refuse to apply a version that has no signature.

reach.task: Use only the signed version of the calculation aid
reach.learn: Which version is signed and which tests the engineer has not accepted

evidence.claim: In a mid-size firm this task is occasional. The engineer specifies the process and reviews the change. A test run that finishes does not show the process is right.
Generated code still needs a person to read the diff. Applying an unsigned draft, or treating a passing run as a sign-off, is out of scope.

assumptions: Focal role is the transportation engineer. The task ends when a signed version is applied to an internal calculation aid. A live signal, a sign controller and a machinery safety function are out of scope.

Input contract: process name, input field names, output field names, sample rows, acceptance test id. Producer is the traffic analyst for the sample, and the engineer for the tests. No sample rows means no generated code.
Use the existing store for the script and its run log before custom code. The meeting prior overstates the task. Agreeing the process is short. The time is the tests, the draft and the review.
A run that completes is recorded as a log only. It is not evidence the code is correct, and it does not replace the review.
unknowns: Who else may apply a signed version.
Whether the aid reads personal trip data.
Which process has no sample rows yet.
research_questions: What share of drafted changes fails a test the engineer wrote?
How often is a signed version rolled back after use?

already_counted.description: Writing the acceptance tests stays with the engineer
Reading the drafted change stays with the engineer
Signing the version stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Revise acceptance tests when a process field changes
Analysts resubmit sample rows the form rejects

approvals.approved_version: software version signed for this process name

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes the process stays as prose with no sample rows, so little code is drafted and the engineer still writes it by hand. The high case assumes a draft appears, while reading the change and signing the version stay with the engineer. A finished test run is not treated as saved review time.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan environmentally sound deconstruction of structures

steps.what: State the obsolete roadways and waste route
Read the condition of the damaged structures

loop.output: rows with material class, quantity and source row id
loop.check: Each quantity cites a source row id on that structure
loop.stop: Leave the quantity blank and stop that line if no source row exists
loop.why_not_simpler: Condition prose is not a fixed waste table

steps.what: Draft plans for the obsolete roadways

loop.input: waste rows and the plan template
loop.output: a sequence whose quantities each cite a source row
loop.check: Every quantity equals a source row already extracted
loop.stop: Drop a line with a quantity that has no source row, then stop
loop.why_not_simpler: The safe order of taking the structure down is not a row lookup

steps.what: Follow the official electronic procedure if waste crosses a border

tasks.design: The asset owner states structure id, condition and whether waste may cross a border. A plan in {DOCS} drafts the sequence and the waste lines only from inspection rows in {SPREADSHEET}. The transportation engineer signs the plan. If that signed plan ships waste across a border, the engineer uses the official electronic procedure. No separate filing portal is built, and a model does not invent a quantity.
tasks.previous_blocker: Condition notes and waste classes were free text, so a plan could not show which row a quantity came from.
tasks.enabler_now: An inspection record can hold material class, quantity and a source row id on the same structure.
tasks.still_hard: How to take a damaged structure down safely, and whether the land is fit for the next use, stays a judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The transportation engineer signs the sequence and the waste route, and starts the official procedure when waste crosses a border.

ambition.what: Name the waste route on every deconstruction plan, not only when a contractor asks

tasks.altitude: Retyping quantities shrinks. The signature does not. The engineer can leave a quantity blank when it has no source row, and can refuse to file an unsigned plan.

reach.task: Follow only the signed sequence and the signed waste line
reach.learn: Which quantities have a source row and whether the official electronic procedure applies

evidence.claim: A deconstruction plan is a sequence plus a waste list. The quantities come from an inspection. The method and the signature stay with the engineer.
Digest [S20] says a paper was withdrawn because the institution did not trust the data. A quantity is filed only when an inspection row supports it. Model-written quantities are not filed.

Digest [S16] says cross-border hazardous-waste procedures have been electronic since 21 May 2026. When the signed plan ships waste across a border, the engineer uses the official electronic procedure. This design does not add a filing portal.

assumptions: Focal role is the transportation engineer. The task ends at the signed plan and, where the plan says so, the start of the official electronic procedure. The contractor's demolition work is out of scope.

Input contract: structure id, condition code, material class, quantity, source row id, crosses-border flag. Producer is the asset owner for the flag and the inspection record for the quantity. A quantity with no source row is left blank.
Use the document template and the inspection table before custom code. Domestic waste is a line on the plan for the contractor. Cross-border waste is not given a workflow of our own.
Many structures do not cross a border. The procedure step is then a recorded no, not a filing.
unknowns: Which waste classes count as hazardous.
Who may sign when the structure is partly on another owner's land.
Whether the inspection quantities are current.
research_questions: What share of plans has a quantity with no source row?
How many plans in a year actually ship waste across a border?

already_counted.description: Engineer checks quantities the extract left blank
Engineer edits the sequence before signing
The plan signature stays with the engineer
The official procedure, when it applies, stays with the engineer

incremental.description: Update the plan template when a new waste class is added
Owners correct a crosses-border flag the request left empty

approvals.approved_version: deconstruction plan signed for this structure id

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low case assumes inspection notes stay as prose, so quantities are still copied by hand and the engineer still writes the sequence. The high case assumes source rows exist, while the method, the signature and any official procedure stay with the engineer. Contractor demolition hours are not treated as saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The transportation engineer reviews generated code and signs deconstruction plans, and neither a finished test run nor a drafted quantity is treated as acceptance.
reach: Tool operators receive only the signed software version, not a draft that merely ran.
Demolition contractors receive the signed plan and the waste line, including whether the official electronic procedure applies.
skills_to_grow: Write the acceptance tests before reading generated code.
Keep deconstruction quantities equal to the inspection record.
Send cross-border waste only through the official electronic procedure.
role.ambitious_version: Internal calculation aids change only by a signed version, and every deconstruction plan names the waste route before work starts.
